taxon_term.notes: Betaproteobacteria capable of dissimilatory vanadium reduction in contaminated mine environments. While not specifically reported in the Panzhihua tailings studies reviewed, Polaromonas is a well-established V(V)-reducing organism in circumneutral pH vanadium mine tailings in northern China and likely present in Panzhihua tailings based on similar environmental conditions (circumneutral pH 6.5-7.5, moderate temperature, high vanadium concentrations). Polaromonas performs dissimilatory V(V) reduction to V(IV) using c-type cytochromes (cymA, omcA) and membrane-associated nitrate reductases (narG). The organism couples oxidation of organic electron donors (lactate, acetate) to V(V) reduction, decreasing vanadium solubility by 2-3 orders of magnitude through precipitation of V(IV) species. This metabolic capacity is critical for vanadium immobilization during anaerobic microsites in revegetated tailings. Polaromonas also reduces Fe(III), Mn(IV), and As(V), contributing to polymetallic redox cycling in V-Ti tailings.

taxon_data.abundance_value: Inferred presence based on V-reducing capacity in similar V-Ti tailings

evidence.snippet: Further, VV-reducing enrichments indicated that bacteria associated with Polaromonas, a genus belonging to the family Burkholderiaceae, were potentially responsible for VV reduction
evidence.explanation: Establishes V(V) reduction mechanism relevant to Panzhihua conditions

taxon_term.notes: Fast-growing nitrogen-fixing rhizobium traditionally associated with pea (Pisum sativum) but adapted to form nodules with P. pinnata in V-Ti tailings. One isolate was identified as R. pisi, demonstrating the promiscuity of rhizobial-legume associations under metal stress conditions. R. pisi contributes to nitrogen enrichment of tailings soil through symbiotic nitrogen fixation and produces plant growth-promoting substances including IAA. The presence of R. pisi indicates that phytoremediation legumes can recruit diverse rhizobial species from indigenous tailings microbiota, not limited to traditional host-specific symbionts. This metabolic flexibility enhances the resilience and effectiveness of legume-rhizobia partnerships in contaminated environments.

evidence.snippet: Based on the phylogenetic analysis of 16S rRNA and four house-keeping genes (atpD, recA, rpoB, glnII), twelve isolates were identified as Bradyrhizobium pachyrhizi, four as Ochrobactrum anthropic, three as Rhizobium selenitireducens and one as Rhizobium pisi
evidence.explanation: Documents R. pisi presence in V-Ti tailings rhizobia

taxon_term.notes: Nitrogen-fixing alphaproteobacterium capable of selenium reduction and heavy metal tolerance, isolated from P. pinnata root nodules in V-Ti tailings. Three isolates were identified as R. selenitireducens, demonstrating nitrogen-fixing capacity and variable tolerance to Cu, Ni, Mn, and Zn. This species possesses unique metabolic capabilities including selenite reduction to elemental selenium, suggesting potential for metalloid detoxification in addition to nitrogen fixation. R. selenitireducens contributes to the functional diversity of the rhizobial community, providing complementary metal tolerance mechanisms and nitrogen enrichment. The organism forms effective symbioses with leguminous plants under metal stress conditions, promoting plant growth through nitrogen provision and IAA production. Like other tailings rhizobia, R. selenitireducens serves as a competent candidate for bioremediation of soils contaminated with multifarious metals due to its combined nitrogen-fixing and metal tolerance phenotypes.

taxon_term.notes: Gram-positive, spore-forming bacteria (Firmicutes phylum) capable of organohalide respiration and metal reduction. Desulfitobacterium species comprise 3-6% of the tailings community and perform dissimilatory reduction of V(V), Cr(VI), and arsenate using respiratory reductases. This genus couples oxidation of hydrogen, formate, lactate, and pyruvate to reduction of electron acceptors including V(V) and sulfite. Desulfitobacterium exhibits greater tolerance to acidic pH (5.5-7.0) and high metal concentrations compared to many deltaproteobacteria, enabling activity in variable tailings microenvironments. Spore formation provides resilience during desiccation or oxidative episodes in surface tailings. The organism expresses reductive dehalogenase homologs (rdhA genes) that reduce V(V) as an alternative electron acceptor. Desulfitobacterium contributes to vanadium reduction particularly in hydrogen-rich microniches generated by fermentative bacteria.

evidence.snippet: Further, VV-reducing enrichments indicated that bacteria associated with Polaromonas, a genus belonging to the family Burkholderiaceae, were potentially responsible for VV reduction
evidence.explanation: Documents presence and enrichment under H₂ amendment

taxon_term.notes: Gram-negative deltaproteobacteria performing dissimilatory sulfate reduction in the vanadium tailings. Desulfovibrio oxidizes organic acids (lactate, pyruvate, formate) and hydrogen coupled to sulfate reduction, producing hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) that chemically reduces V(V) to V(IV) and precipitates vanadium as sulfide minerals. Additionally, Desulfovibrio can enzymatically reduce V(V) through periplasmic and cytoplasmic reductases. The organism comprises 8-12% of the tailings community and increases under sulfate-rich, organic-amended conditions. Hydrogen sulfide generated by Desulfovibrio (concentrations reaching 50-200 µM) creates strongly reducing microenvironments (Eh < -200 mV) that favor vanadium immobilization. Desulfovibrio species are known to reduce multiple toxic metals including uranium, chromium, and technetium, contributing to polymetallic remediation in this system.

taxon_term.notes: Deltaproteobacteria specialized in dissimilatory metal reduction, present at 5-8% relative abundance in vanadium tailings. Geobacter oxidizes acetate and other organic acids coupled to reduction of Fe(III), Mn(IV), and V(V). This genus possesses extensive arrays of c-type cytochromes enabling extracellular electron transfer to metal oxides and soluble metal ions. In vanadium tailings, Geobacter reduces co-occurring Fe(III) minerals, creating reducing conditions that facilitate V(V) reduction by other community members. Geobacter can directly reduce V(V) through outer membrane cytochromes (OmcB, OmcS, OmcZ) and periplasmic reductases. The organism is particularly important in zones with high Fe(III) content (common in vanadium titanomagnetite tailings), where Fe(III) reduction precedes and enhances V(V) reduction. Geobacter forms syntrophic relationships with Polaromonas, potentially exchanging electrons or metabolites.
